summary: ISO 8601 duration support for ms: formatISO is committed and parseISO, its inverse, is added with round-trip tests. Both are exported from src/index.ts. No PR merge or release is recorded yet.
narrative: On Nov 2 the owner asked for ISO 8601 duration formatting in ms, with days as the largest unit and tests. formatISO was added with its own test file and committed as e2ceaf8 (obs 2, 3). The owner noted that a security reviewer wants no regular expressions in new parsing code on this branch, so the parse side had to be hand-written. About seven minutes later a new conversation continued with parseISO as the inverse of formatISO. parseISO was added in src/index.ts, handling weeks, days and time parts, optional sign, and comma or dot decimals. It returns NaN for years and months. A trailing-T case such as "P1DT" was fixed to be rejected (obs 16, 17). A parseISO test suite with formatISO round-trips was added and the full suite passed at 188 tests (obs 18). Memory shows no commit of parseISO, PR merge, release or owner confirmation yet, so the work is in review-ready state, not shipped. One open question is that the later observations mention a /t$/i test, which sits uneasily with the no-regex constraint.
